tasks.title: Flow test, name scan and docs
tasks.summary: One end-to-end flow test over the merged pieces, a hermetic scan of the project names in every added file, and the operator and router docs for `/bs use`.
tasks.objective: Prove the whole flow once over the merged work of task-1 to task-5 and document it: a flow test drives `/bs use`, a follow-up prompt, a bypass answer and the projection in one temp store, plus runs of the built hook binding the factory's own name; a hermetic test scans every file this plan adds for project names outside the placeholders; the operator docs gain the `/bs use` verb, the reminder, the policy file, the bypass record and the dashboard label, and the router files list the verb.
acceptance_criteria: Epic criteria 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9 together, in factory/orchestrator/test/sessionBindingFlow.test.ts (new), in process with a temp factory-shaped checkout and a temp roadmap declaring project-a and project-b: capturePrompt on `/bs use project-a`, then bindingReminder on a follow-up prompt returns lines naming project-a; the follow-up user_prompt carries project-a; every home-log user_prompt after the binding carries payload.bound_to = the session-bound event's id, and bindingFromTail over the log's records with the session-bound record removed still returns project-a; a bypass answer adds one pipeline-bypass-approved event carrying its question; after projecting the log into a temp db, cliSessionBindings names project-a for the cli id and the timeline holds both new types.

Epic criteria 1, 5 and 11, built hook: dist/promptHook.js run on `/bs use ` followed by FACTORY_PROJECT_NAME (imported, never typed) in a temp M2 checkout exits 0, prints the capture line and reminder lines naming that project and no JSON line, and leaves exactly one session-bound event in that checkout's home log; a follow-up prompt prints the reminder again and its user_prompt carries that project.

Epic criterion 12 (documented): README.md's subcommand table and docs/guide/operator-loop.md's table gain a `/bs use <project>` row; docs/guide/operator-loop.md gains a short section on binding a session (what the operator types, what the reminder says, that nothing blocks, where the size numbers live and how an operator overrides them, what the reminder says when the policy file is missing or invalid, how the yes is recorded and that the question names the change, what the dashboard shows); the 'Putting your own words in the log' paragraph of docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md names the session-bound and pipeline-bypass-approved events, the home-log filing rule, and that `bs event append` refuses both types; the `/bs` verb list on CLAUDE.md line 42 and in the AGENTS.md router-table row for the operator console gains `use`; the 'Live sessions' section of docs/guide/dashboard.md says a bound session's card shows the bound project, ahead of a linked epic's.

Test first: the flow test is written before the docs and run on the branch carrying task-1 to task-5; under the null (main at 1cdb9aaf) it fails at the import of sessionBinding.ts and bindingReminder.ts; after the plan it passes. test/docCommands.test.ts and test/operatorLanguage.test.ts pass over the edited docs.

Text proof: the edited docs, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/guide/dashboard.md included, name no project except through <project> placeholders, hold no absolute path, and restate no number from factory/policies/session-binding.yml.

Epic criterion 11 (mechanical part), in factory/orchestrator/test/sessionBindingNames.test.ts (new), reading repo files only: it lists the files this plan adds (factory/orchestrator/src/sessionBinding.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/sessionBinding.test.ts, factory/policies/session-binding.yml, factory/orchestrator/test/promptCaptureBinding.test.ts, factory/orchestrator/src/bindingReminder.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/bindingReminder.test.ts, .claude/skills/bs/use.md, factory/orchestrator/test/skillUse.test.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/eventAppendHookOnly.test.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/db/cliSessionBinding.test.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/sessionBindingFlow.test.ts) and asserts each exists. In every file this plan adds or edits it reads each `/bs use` argument (the token after `/bs use` and spaces, made of letters, digits, `<`, `>`, `_`, `.` and `-`); in the added files it also reads each `project:` or `"project":` value given as a quoted string and each `- project:` line's value. Every value read is project-a, project-b or <project>, plus nothing-here for a `/bs use` argument; a value starting with `$` and an unquoted identifier are skipped. A positive control runs the same readers on inline samples: `/bs use other-name`, `project: 'other-name'` and `- project: other-name` give three hits, and `/bs use <project>`, `project: name` and `project: '${x}'` give none. The file excludes itself from the scan. Under the null the added files are absent and the existence assertion fails; revert proof: put `/bs use other-name` in use.md and the scan fails.
Gates: `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test` in full, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full.

functional_clauses: The docs describe behaviour as task-1 to task-5 shipped it; a gap between a doc and the code is raised as a finding against the owning task, not papered over in prose.
Each doc gets its own row or section; no doc restates another doc's section, and the operator-loop section links use.md rather than copying it.
The built-hook case reads only its temp checkout's store and asserts nothing about which other names the shipped roadmap declares.
CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md change only by adding `use` to the existing verb lists; the dashboard.md edit is limited to the live-session card's project in its 'Live sessions' section.

The name scan is hermetic: it reads the listed repo files and its inline samples only, never a roadmap, the overlay, factoryProjects or git history, so it gives the same result on CI and on a workstation. The edited files it scans for `/bs use` arguments are the files task-1 to task-6 claim that already exist at 1cdb9aaf.
nonfunctional_clauses: Exported names and signatures stay as they are.
Edit only the claimed files; a needed edit outside them stops the task with error.spec.spec-gap.
In the worktree, symlink the main clone's node_modules; stage files by name and never run `git add -A`.

English only; no absolute paths and no other project names. A project value in a file this plan adds (a `project:` or `"project":` value, a `- project:` roadmap line, a `/bs use` argument) is project-a or project-b, or <project> in prose; the unknown name in a `/bs use` example is nothing-here; epic-a, epic-b, store-a, store-b, demo-hub and blacksmith name epics, stores, hubs and checkouts, never a project; the factory's own name is read from FACTORY_PROJECT_NAME, never typed.

Tests build their fixtures in temp dirs (temp checkouts and stores, a temp db, a fake CLI session id), read no git history, and never read the real session registry, the user's home config directory or the real state/ store.
No doc describes a binding as a block, a hold or a permission; it is a record and a reminder.
Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full as the final gate; quote its tail and name every SKIP.

tasks.title: Bound-session fixes
tasks.summary: A bad home log no longer loses a prompt; an unlinked bound card names its project; the two binding titles drop the 'a project' placeholder.
tasks.objective: Fix the three wave-2 defects the operator kept inside this epic (2026-10-16), branching from the integration head 107be5f3. (1) Spec finding f-bs-use/integration-7efdb20c, closing f-bs-use/task-2-capture-writes-binding-2aee7558: in factory/orchestrator/src/promptCapture.ts the newest-binding read of the home log `prompts-<cli>` (line 356) and the `/bs use` binding append before it are unguarded, so a malformed or unreadable home log makes capturePrompt reject and a prompt bound for a live epic log is never filed; a binding that cannot be read now counts as no binding for that prompt, and the prompt reaches its target. (2) Spec finding f-bs-use/integration-9edcd723, closing f-bs-use/followup-60e5fdbb-60e5fdbb: task-5 ui-spec SPEC GAP option (a) in ui/src/lib/liveSessions.ts, so the live card of a session bound with `/bs use <project>` but linked to no open epic names the bound project the server already sends as card.project, and still says it is not linked. (3) Spec finding f-bs-use/integration-47ed5c39, closing f-bs-use/followup-6bc620bc-6bc620bc: ui/src/lib/timelineDisplay.ts lines 380 and 382 fall back to the bare phrase of ui-spec section 2 instead of 'a project' when payload.project is missing or empty.
acceptance_criteria: Defect 1 (epic criteria 2 and 5), in factory/orchestrator/test/promptCaptureBinding.test.ts, in a new describe 'a home log that cannot be read', case 'a malformed home log does not stop a prompt reaching its epic log': in the file's m2 setup, write `prompts-<CLI>.jsonl` in m2.dir holding one line that is not JSON, call seedEpicLog(m2.dir, 'project-b'), then say(m2, 'into the epic'). capturePrompt resolves, not rejects, to the `bs prompt capture:` line whose session_id is epic-b-main; the epic-b-main log holds that user_prompt with project project-b and no payload.bound_to; no log holds a pipeline-bypass-approved event; the home log's bytes are unchanged. The same case repeats with the home log path made a directory (unreadable) and expects the same outcome. Null proof: on 107be5f3 capturePrompt rejects (events.unreadable-session-log for the bad line, EISDIR for the directory), so the case fails. Revert proof: put the unguarded read back at the newest-binding lookup and this case fails, while the criterion 3 guard and every defect 2 and defect 3 case still pass.

Defect 1, the `/bs use` turn, same describe, case 'a /bs use turn with a malformed home log files the prompt and binds nothing': malformed home log as in criterion 1, seedEpicLog(m2.dir, 'project-b'), then use(m2, 'project-a'). capturePrompt resolves to the line naming epic-b-main; epic-b-main holds the `/bs use project-a` user_prompt with project project-b and no payload.bound_to; no log holds a session-bound event; the home log's bytes are unchanged. Null proof: on 107be5f3 the binding append throws first and capturePrompt rejects, so the case fails. Revert proof: remove the guard around the `/bs use` binding append and this case fails while criterion 1's case still passes; remove the read guard and both fail. The home log as the target, same describe, case 'guard (passes before and after): a malformed home log that is itself the target refuses the prompt as before task-2': seed no epic log, so the home log is the prompt's target, and write the home log as in criterion 1; say(m2, 'here') and then use(m2, 'project-a') each reject with an error whose code is 'events.unreadable-session-log'; the home log's bytes are unchanged and no other `.jsonl` log appears in m2.dir, so no user_prompt or session-bound event is written anywhere. This is the outcome at 1cdb9aaf (main before task-2): `write(home)` reads the log through appendWithin, readEventsAtPath throws 'events.unreadable-session-log' on the first line, and capturePrompt rethrows (`if (target === home) throw err;`), as the existing promptCapture.test.ts case 'a failing home log still throws, with no second retry' already pins for an unwritable home log; the hook entries swallow the throw, exit 0 and print nothing (promptHookEntry.test.ts, 'guard: an internal failure (a home log line that is not JSON) exits 0 and prints nothing'). This behaviour is pre-existing and out of this task's scope: the fix does not file this prompt in another log, retry, or repair, rewrite or skip a malformed line, and neither a coder nor a judge widens the task to do so. The guard passes on 107be5f3 (the newest-binding read, or for `/bs use` the binding append, throws the same code first) and after the fix (the guarded reads yield no binding, then the home write throws). Revert proof: a change that files the prompt elsewhere, swallows the home write's throw or touches the home log fails this guard.

Defect 1 no-regression guard, same describe, case 'guard (passes before and after): a well-formed home log binding is still read': use(m2, 'project-a'), then say(m2, 'here') files a home-log user_prompt with project project-a and payload.bound_to equal to the session-bound event's id; then seedEpicLog(m2.dir, 'project-b') and a yes answer to the bypass question (the file's `answer` fixture in answer mode, prompt id toolu_9) leaves exactly one pipeline-bypass-approved event in epic-b-main. It passes on 107be5f3 and after the change. Revert proof: make the guarded read always yield no binding and this guard fails, as does the existing case 'the event follows the answer into an epic log and takes that log project'. Every existing case in the file keeps its expectations unchanged.

Defect 2 (epic criterion 9, ui-spec section 1 and SPEC GAP (a)), in ui/test/liveSessions.test.ts, describe 'liveCardView title', new case 'names the bound project ahead of the working folder when unlinked': card({ project: 'project-a', name: 'fix login' }) (focus null) gives title 'project-a · workspace-c', titleMuted ' · fix login', meta 'Not linked to a Blacksmith epic', titleLink null, now [] and next null. Null proof: on 107be5f3 the title is 'workspace-c', so the case fails. Revert proof: drop the project read in the no-focus branch of liveCardView and this case fails while the criterion 5 guard, the existing focus-branch cases and every defect 1 and defect 3 case still pass.

Defect 2 guard, same describe, case 'guard (passes before and after): an unlinked card without a bound project reads as before, and a folder named like the project shows it once': with project absent, null and '' the unlinked title is 'workspace-c' and holds no 'null', 'undefined' or leading separator, with titleMuted and meta as the existing case 'is the working-folder label plus a muted session name when unlinked' expects; card({ project: 'project-a', cwdLabel: 'project-a' }) gives title 'project-a'. It passes on 107be5f3 and after the change. Revert proof: drop the same-name check and this guard fails ('project-a · project-a') while criterion 4 and the comparison case below still pass. The same-name rule is an exact, case-sensitive comparison between the bound project and the card's whole cwdLabel, with no trimming, case folding or path splitting; same describe, case 'compares the bound project with the whole working-folder label, exactly and case-sensitively': card({ project: 'project-a', cwdLabel: 'Project-A' }) gives title 'project-a · Project-A', and card({ project: 'project-a', cwdLabel: 'apps/project-a' }) gives 'project-a · apps/project-a'. This case is not a guard: on 107be5f3 the titles are 'Project-A' and 'apps/project-a', so it fails (null proof). Revert proof: make the comparison case-folded or compare only the label's last path segment and this case fails while the guard above and criterion 4 still pass. The existing cases in the file keep their expectations unchanged.

Defect 2 rendered, in ui/e2e/home.spec.ts, describe 'Home: Live sessions', new test 'a bound unlinked session names its project and stays not linked': serveLive(page, liveResponse({ sessions: [liveCard({ cliSessionId: 'cli-3', status: 'idle', statusSince: null, name: 'session-c', project: 'project-a' })] })); on /overview that list item contains 'project-a · workspace-c · session-c' and 'Not linked to a Blacksmith epic', shows no Now or Next line and holds no link; at the file's PHONE viewport the page has no sideways scroll and the title's box stays inside the card's box. LIVE_CARDS gets no project, so the existing test 'an unlinked session shows its folder, name and no Now or Next' and the 'screenshot live sessions' loop keep their fixtures and pass unchanged. Null proof: on 107be5f3 the item reads 'workspace-c · session-c', so the text check fails. Revert proof: the criterion 4 revert fails this test too.

Visual pass (uiux, kind visual), at desktop 1280 and phone 390, each in light and dark. Live-card view, sourced from the criterion 6 e2e fixture and shot with the e2e suite's headless Playwright chromium: the home live card of a bound unlinked session reads 'project-a · workspace-c' with the muted ' · session-c' and the meta line 'Not linked to a Blacksmith epic'; the title is plain text, not a link; no badge, chip, button, icon or style is added; a long title wraps or ellipsizes as an unlinked title does at 107be5f3 and nothing overflows the card at 390; the card's height, padding and alignment match an unbound unlinked card's. Timeline view, sourced from a fixture the tester builds, because the binding writer always stamps payload.project and no claimed fixture renders a project-less binding row: a temp BS_HOME made at run time under the OS temp dir, whose state/events holds one hand-written log `prompts-<fake CLI id>.jsonl` with a session-start root, a session-bound event and a pipeline-bypass-approved event that carry no payload.project, and a session-bound event whose payload.project is project-b, every line with top-level project project-a. The project-less events stand for older or hand-written records the titles must still handle. Beside it a temp roadmap declares project-a and project-b, and an empty temp directory stands in for the CLI config directory. From the task worktree, after `pnpm run build:server` and `pnpm run build:ui`, the tester runs `node factory/orchestrator/dist/cli.js db rebuild` and then `node factory/orchestrator/dist/cli.js ui serve`, with BS_HOME set to the temp home, `--db`, `--state-dir` and `--roadmap-path` naming the temp files, `--claude-config-dir` naming the empty directory, and `--port` a free port outside 4680-4683; opens the Activity page (/activity) on project-a; shoots it with the same headless Playwright chromium as the live-card view; and stops only the server it started. That timeline shows rows titled 'Session bound' and 'Pipeline bypass approved' with the Prompt tag, each on one line with no trailing separator and no 'a project', 'undefined' or 'null', beside the named row 'Session bound to project-b', which reads as before. Any helper script is untracked inside the task worktree and removed before hand-back; nothing outside the claims is committed, and no claim is added for this pass. No new interactive element is added, so no new touch target is measured.

Defect 3 (epic criterion 8, ui-spec section 2), in ui/test/timelineDisplay.test.ts, describe 'session binding events', new case 'titles session-bound with the bare phrase when no project is named': for payload {}, { project: null } and { project: '' }, titleFor(entry({ eventType: 'session-bound', payload })) is exactly 'Session bound': no trailing space, no 'a project', 'undefined' or 'null'. Null proof: on 107be5f3 it reads 'Session bound to a project' or 'Session bound to ', so the case fails. Revert proof: restore line 380 as it was and this case fails while criterion 9 and the existing named-project cases still pass.

Defect 3, same describe, case 'titles pipeline-bypass-approved with the bare phrase when no project is named': the same three payloads give exactly 'Pipeline bypass approved' under the same checks. Null proof: on 107be5f3 it reads 'Pipeline bypass approved for a project' or 'Pipeline bypass approved for ', so the case fails. Revert proof: restore line 382 as it was and this case fails while criterion 8 and the existing named-project cases still pass. The existing cases 'titles session-bound by the project it names', 'titles pipeline-bypass-approved by the project it names' and 'gives both the prompt kind' keep their expectations unchanged.

Test first: every new case in the four test files is written before the fix. Under the null (107be5f3) the cases of criteria 1, 4, 6, 8 and 9, the first case of criterion 2 and the comparison case of criterion 5 fail, and the guards of criteria 2, 3 and 5 pass; after the fix all pass. Quote both runs' case lines in the result.

Gates: `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run test` in full, `pnpm run test:server`, `pnpm run test:ui`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run typecheck:server`, `pnpm run typecheck:ui`, `pnpm run typecheck:ui:test`, `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full, which runs `pnpm run test:e2e` when chromium is installed; if it prints SKIP for the e2e step, run `pnpm run test:e2e` once by hand or report the skip by name.

functional_clauses: promptCapture.ts: the newest-binding read of the home log runs inside a try/catch, and any throw (a malformed line, an unreadable path) leaves `bound` undefined for that prompt. The `/bs use` binding append runs inside a try/catch, and a throw writes no binding while the prompt goes on to its target. Nothing else in capturePrompt changes: the target choice, the epic-log fallback to the home log, the dedupe, the binding read inside `write` for a home-log target, the bound_to stamp and the bypass record stay as they are at 107be5f3.

A malformed home log that is itself the prompt's target keeps the behaviour it had before task-2 (1cdb9aaf): capturePrompt rejects with 'events.unreadable-session-log', the hook entries swallow it, and the prompt is not filed (criterion 2's guard). Repairing, rewriting or skipping a malformed log is out of this task's scope; this task changes only the paths where the home log is read for a binding.
The capture fix adds no retry, wait, lock, extra read or stdout line, and never repairs, rewrites or deletes the home log.

liveSessions.ts: LiveCard gains an optional `project?: string | null`, the CliSessionCard.project the server already sends. In liveCardView's no-focus branch a non-empty string project becomes the first part of the title, `<project> · <cwdLabel>`, or `<project>` alone when the whole cwdLabel is exactly equal to it (case-sensitive; no trimming, case folding or path splitting). titleMuted, meta ('Not linked to a Blacksmith epic'), titleLink, titleLabel, titleTooltip, now, moreCount and next stay as they are. With project absent, null or '', the view is exactly what it is at 107be5f3. The UI does not normalize the name again; the server sends it normalized.

The focus branch of liveCardView is unchanged: the server already sets focus.project from the binding (ui-spec option (b), task-5). LiveSessionCard.vue and ui/server/src/cliSessions.ts are not edited.

timelineDisplay.ts: when payload.project is a non-empty string, the session-bound and pipeline-bypass-approved titles stay 'Session bound to <project>' and 'Pipeline bypass approved for <project>'; otherwise they are the bare 'Session bound' and 'Pipeline bypass approved'. kindFor, metaFor and every other title are unchanged. TimelineRow.vue, RunHistoryTimeline.vue and agentStatus.ts inherit the titles and are not edited.

keeps_exports: promptCapture.ts, liveSessions.ts and timelineDisplay.ts only add; every existing export keeps its name and signature, and LiveCard's new field is optional so every existing LiveCard literal still type-checks.
The visible change is the title of a bound unlinked live card and the two timeline titles when no project is named; no new component, style, token, route, interactive element or write path.
